title: Exodus
author: Moses is traditionally understood as the author of Exodus as part of the Pentateuch.
date: Traditionally connected with the time of Moses and Israel's deliverance from Egypt.
audience: The people of Israel, called to remember the Lord's deliverance, covenant, worship, and presence among them.
historicalSetting: Exodus records Israel's bondage in Egypt, God's raising up of Moses, the plagues, the Passover, the crossing of the Red Sea, the giving of the law at Sinai, and the construction of the tabernacle.
themes: Deliverance by the power of God
The Passover and redemption by blood
Worship and the presence of God
The Lord dwelling among His people
keyVerse: Exodus 12:13 — "When I see the blood, I will pass over you."
christFocus: Exodus points to Christ through the Passover lamb, redemption from bondage, the mediator Moses, the manna from heaven, the water from the rock, and the tabernacle where God dwelt among His people. Christ is the true Passover Lamb and the final Mediator who delivers His people from sin.
outline: Israel's bondage and the birth of Moses — Exodus 1-2
The call of Moses and confrontation with Pharaoh — Exodus 3-11
Passover and deliverance from Egypt — Exodus 12-15
The wilderness journey to Sinai — Exodus 16-18
The covenant and law at Sinai — Exodus 19-24
The tabernacle instructions and construction — Exodus 25-40
